A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MAP research and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Matching relocated material and inspecting rendered figures supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original model-merging experiments, including vision and language results, baseline comparisons, surrogate-fit analyses, and nested and Bayesian MAP evaluations.

after.justification: v4 retains original model-merging experiments and additionally reports task-vector magnitude measurements and Pareto-distance curves.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 moves coefficient sampling from inside the per-task loop to before it, specifying a shared coefficient set across tasks. This changes the stated sampling procedure. Quadratic and warped surrogates, Pareto search, nested merging and Bayesian updates otherwise remain intact.

E1.justification: The eight standard vision datasets, NIH chest-X-ray tasks, four language evaluations, and ResNet classification tasks remain. Added and removed analyses concern existing data and model-merging tasks rather than new domains, populations or task coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator set remains: direct search, SLERP, TIES, DARE combinations, Task Arithmetic variants, Model Soups and MTL. The retained comparisons preserve comparator membership. Removing the preference-win-rate block from v3 Table 3 does not remove these methods from the corresponding accuracy comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes front-win-rate sampling from K=min(100,|PFbaseline|) to K=100; unchanged reported scores do not establish that experiments were rerun. v4 also adds a GD/IGD sampling-budget sweep and removes the preference-wise baseline win-rate evaluation and four-task constrained-merging protocol. Main model configurations and benchmark budgets remain.

E4.justification: v4 adds task-vector magnitude diagnostics in Section 2.3 and GD/IGD sensitivity to sampling budget in Figure 7. It removes v3's out-of-sample R2 budget sweep for two through seven tasks and the rule-based four-task nested-versus-direct comparison. These substantially change the analyses supporting surrogate validity and nested-merging trade-offs.

E5.justification: Neither version introduces different repeated-run or seed disclosures. Standard-deviation reporting remains, as do Bayesian bootstrap settings of 20% dropping and 30 samples. Added or removed result entries do not establish a changed uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Main benchmark table values are retained, but substantial diagnostic and comparative results change. v4 adds task-vector L1 ratios of 1.07–1.66% and GD/IGD curves, while removing preference win rates, constrained four-task accuracies, R2 sensitivity curves and the Cars–SUN397 baseline-comparison panel. Section 3.3 also newly asserts a 250× speedup without a clearly supporting reported comparison.

T1.justification: v4 introduces explicit Assumption 1 concerning relative task-vector size and metric smoothness, plus Corollaries 1 and 3 spelling out the regression design matrix and normal-equation solution. v3 already described linear-regression fitting. The Pareto definitions, Taylor-remainder proof and nested-merging complexity derivation are retained.

C1.justification: The central quadratic-surrogate MAP contribution and its Bayesian and nested variants remain. However, v4 removes the conclusion-level restriction to convex-front approximation and asserts non-convex-front coverage in Appendix F.2, broadening the claimed applicability.

C2.justification: v3 says MAP cannot handle non-convex fronts and approximates their convex hull; v4 instead explains that NSGA-III permits non-convex coverage. v4 also interprets new magnitude measurements as validating the Taylor assumption, narrows Bayesian MAP's recommended range from N≤4 to N≤3, and removes the federated/model-privacy discussion.

D1.justification: v4 explicitly states that gradient descent fits sigmoid- and softplus-wrapped surrogates, whereas v3 lists several possible solvers. The optional MAE/Huber and alternative-solver discussion is removed. Repository access, checkpoint identifiers, memory examples, ResNet head fine-tuning and Bayesian hyperparameters remain; the new solver specificity is documentation rather than evidence of changed experiments.

R1.justification: v4 adds Chung et al. (2024) and Merlin et al. (2023) to support its fine-tuning motivation and expands the contrast with linear scalarization. Most cited research remains, with existing related work condensed into Section 5. Explicit federated/private-learning positioning is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, method exposition and conclusion are rewritten, and the narrative is substantially reorganized. Detailed variant descriptions move to consolidated appendices, related work gains a main-text section, and notation, motivation, formal cases and reorganized Q&A improve navigation.

P2.justification: v4 redraws the pipeline and Bayesian schematic, adds magnitude, notation, discretization and GD/IGD displays, and splits the original front-win-rate table. It removes a comparison panel, R2 plots, the rule-based table and a win-rate block. Extensive resizing, relocation and table styling accompany the new document layout.

improvement.justification: v4 improves organization and surrogate-fitting explanations and adds useful magnitude and Pareto-distance diagnostics. However, it removes high-dimensional fit-sensitivity evidence, constrained-merging results and preference win rates. Its new 250× speedup assertion lacks a clearly identified supporting comparison; the retained nested-versus-plain experiment reports 480 versus 2240 evaluations. These benefits and evidential weaknesses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
